name: article
description: Long-form reading layout composing a header (badge eyebrow, headline, standfirst, avatar byline), a cover image, the prose body with pull quotes, a sticky table of contents and a footer of tags and share links. Composition only: zero JavaScript, no controller, no reactive directives — the two layouts are pure CSS grid.

header.description: The masthead of the piece: eyebrow, headline, summary and byline stacked in one grid

eyebrow.description: Short kicker above the headline, inside the header — typically holds a nested data-ui='badge'

headline.description: The title of the piece, in the heading voice. Give it an id and point the article's aria-labelledby at it so the article is named

summary.description: The standfirst under the headline: one size up from the body and muted

byline.description: One row inside the header: a nested data-ui='avatar', then the author and meta parts

author.description: The author's name, inside the byline

meta.description: Date and reading time, inside the byline. Put the date in a <time datetime> so it is machine-readable

cover.description: Wrapper for the cover picture — a nested data-ui='image' figure, which keeps its own caption

body.description: The prose: ordinary paragraphs, h2/h3 headings, lists and figures in block flow. Only the measure and the vertical rhythm are set by the pattern. A nested data-ui='quote' with data-variant='pull' may sit between paragraphs

aside.description: Table of contents: a nested data-ui='nav' data-variant='vertical' labelled 'On this page'. The sidebar layout pins it beside the body from the lg floor

footer.description: Closing row under a hairline, holding the tags and share parts

tags.description: Topic tags inside the footer, each a nested data-ui='badge'

share.description: Share links inside the footer, each a nested data-ui='link' with real link text

--article-measure.description: Maximum inline size of the body prose (custom property). Pass a measure token; the default is the prose measure, sized in characters so it tracks the reader's font.

required_attrs: aria-labelledby on the article pointing at the headline id
alt text on the cover image and on any avatar image in the byline
aria-label on the aside and on the nested table-of-contents nav
datetime on the <time> inside the meta part
a11y.notes: The headline is the page's h1; headings inside the body start at h2 and never skip a level. The table of contents is a navigation landmark of its own inside a complementary landmark, so both carry a name. The reading-progress bar, when composed in, is aria-hidden: the browser's own scrollbar already reports position.

keyboard.Tab: move through the table-of-contents links, the links inside the prose and the share links in source order

templates.html:
{eyebrow}

{headline}

{summary}

{initials} {author} {date} · {reading_time}
{body}
{tag}
{share_label}

notes: Nested primitives inside a slot keep their own five-attribute contract and must not carry a data-part: the badge sits inside [data-part="eyebrow"] or [data-part="tags"], the avatar inside [data-part="byline"], the image figure inside [data-part="cover"], the vertical nav inside [data-part="aside"].
[data-part="cover"] is a <div> that wraps the image primitive, not a <figure>: the primitive already is the figure, with its own caption part, and two nested figures would announce one picture twice.

The body is ordinary HTML in block flow. The pattern sets its measure, its type size and the rhythm between direct children — paragraphs, h2/h3 headings, lists, figures — and nothing inside them. A pull quote is the quote primitive with data-variant="pull" placed between two paragraphs.

A reading-progress bar is composition, not a prop: put ONE
as the first child of the article and it pins itself to the top of the page. The pattern itself does nothing for it.

The sidebar layout is the single centred column below the lg floor — a 16rem rail beside the prose on a phone would starve the text — and the aside is a plain block after the body there. From lg the header, cover and footer span both columns and the aside sits in the end column, sticky at --space-8 from the top.
Headings inside the body that the table of contents links to carry ids: an anchor needs a target, and that is the one reason an id appears inside the prose.
